subject: Civil Engineering
title: Buttress Dams
description: A quick, practical guide to Buttress Dams.

hook.text: A flat wall can't hold back a river alone — but lean supports on the downstream side can.

buildup.text: Buttress dams have a thin upstream face supported by triangular walls — buttresses — behind.

discovery.text: They use 30-50% less concrete than gravity dams — the buttresses transfer loads efficiently.

twist.text: Each buttress works independently — damage to one doesn't compromise the entire structure.

climax.text: Daniel-Johnson Dam in Canada — the world's largest multiple-arch buttress dam.

punchline.text: A thin wall with strong legs — buttress dams trade mass for smart engineering.

quiz.question: What advantage do buttress dams have over gravity dams?
options: They can be built in wider valleys with weaker rock foundations
They use 30-50% less concrete by using triangular supports instead of solid mass
They generate more hydroelectric power due to increased water flow
